schema_diff_discrimination_gap.description: Mean schema diff magnitude for drift patterns (0.96) minus mean for noise patterns (0.59)

c1_drift_detection_mean_diff.description: Mean schema diff magnitude across all drift patterns and all schema sizes

c2_noise_tolerance_mean_diff.description: Mean schema diff magnitude across all noise patterns and all schema sizes
c2_noise_tolerance_mean_diff.primary_violation: optional_field_addition noise pattern produces diff magnitude that scales with schema size (1.0 at n=10, 2.0 at n=20, 3.0 at n=30, 5.0 at n=50)

c3_orthogonality_pearson_r.description: Pearson correlation between schema diff magnitude and Jaccard structural similarity across all 40 conditions
c3_orthogonality_pearson_r.interpretation: Schema diff is negatively correlated with Jaccard (diff increases as Jaccard decreases), indicating schema diff captures complementary structural information

c4_type_aware_validation_rate.description: Profile C (heavy validation: type+required+enum) failure rate for change_type pattern at n=50
c4_type_aware_validation_rate.interpretation: Mock server always returns data matching schema types, so type-aware client validation never detects type drift. Only 4.7% failure rate from required-field removal side effects.

CTRL-JACCARD-STRUCTURAL.description: Jaccard similarity on (field_name, type) pairs between fresh and stale schemas
CTRL-JACCARD-STRUCTURAL.expected_behavior: Degrades with drift; unchanged by description/nesting noise; degrades with optional_field_addition
CTRL-JACCARD-STRUCTURAL.observed_behavior: Drift patterns: 0.818-1.0; Noise: 0.909-1.0 (all noise patterns similar)
CTRL-JACCARD-STRUCTURAL.key_finding: Cannot discriminate optional_field_addition noise from add_field drift (both produce Jaccard ~0.909)

CTRL-RESPONSE-TIME-KS.description: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on response time distributions
CTRL-RESPONSE-TIME-KS.expected_behavior: Cannot detect any schema-only drift (mock server is deterministic)
CTRL-RESPONSE-TIME-KS.observed_behavior: Not directly computed (mock server produces zero latency variance)
CTRL-RESPONSE-TIME-KS.key_finding: Already falsified in parent EXP-GRAPH-35137034388; not re-tested in this experiment

CTRL-LDA-ENSEMBLE.description: Linear Fisher LDA ensemble combining multiple signals
CTRL-LDA-ENSEMBLE.observed_behavior: Not directly computed; schema diff alone achieves 0.37 discrimination gap
CTRL-LDA-ENSEMBLE.key_finding: Previous best AUC=0.625 used indirect signals; schema diff does not improve on this

CTRL-FIELD-USAGE-PROFILING.expected_behavior: Orthogonal to Jaccard but shares magnitude confound
CTRL-FIELD-USAGE-PROFILING.observed_behavior: Not re-tested; parent experiment confirmed r=-0.045 with Jaccard
CTRL-FIELD-USAGE-PROFILING.key_finding: Parent established that usage-based signals are orthogonal to schema-based signals

CTRL-POISSON-NULL.description: Poisson noise signal (baseline from experiment design)
CTRL-POISSON-NULL.observed_behavior: Not directly computed in this experiment

CTRL-NOISE-TAUTOLOGICAL-FIX.description: Noise patterns redesigned to overlap with client-requested fields (fixing V_NOISE_TAUTOLOGICAL)
CTRL-NOISE-TAUTOLOGICAL-FIX.expected_behavior: Noise patterns that overlap client fields should produce measurable diff magnitude
CTRL-NOISE-TAUTOLOGICAL-FIX.observed_behavior: description_change: 0.0 (invisible to schema diff); default_value_change: 0.0 (invisible); optional_field_addition: 1.0-5.0 (visible but scales with size); nested_property_addition: 0.0 (invisible); enum_expansion: 0.2 (visible)
CTRL-NOISE-TAUTOLOGICAL-FIX.key_finding: 3 of 5 noise patterns are invisible to schema diff (description, default_value, nested_property); 2 are visible (optional_addition, enum_expansion)

observations.description: Schema diff magnitude distinguishes drift from noise for 4 of 5 noise patterns
observations.evidence: Drift mean=0.96, Noise mean=0.59. 4 noise patterns produce diff=0.0 (description_change, default_value_change, nested_property_addition are invisible to field-name/type/required comparison). Only optional_field_addition (diff=1.0-5.0) and enum_expansion (diff=0.2) produce nonzero diff.

observations.description: optional_field_addition noise produces diff magnitude that scales with schema size, creating irreconcilable threshold conflict
observations.evidence: At n=10: diff=1.0; n=20: diff=2.0; n=30: diff=3.0; n=50: diff=5.0. Meanwhile drift patterns produce constant diff magnitudes (add_field=1.0, remove_field=1.0, change_type=0.5, required_to_optional=0.3, rename_field=2.0). A threshold that catches required_to_optional (0.3) would also catch optional_field_addition at n=10 (1.0).

observations.description: rename_field produces the highest schema diff magnitude (2.0) but zero client validation failures
observations.evidence: rename_field diff=2.0 (add 1 + remove 1) across all sizes; all client validation rates=0.0. The diff measures structural change but clients don't validate field names.

observations.description: required_to_optional is the only drift pattern invisible to Jaccard but visible to schema diff
observations.evidence: required_to_optional: Jaccard=1.0 (unchanged), schema diff=0.3. All other drift patterns produce Jaccard < 1.0. This is the one case where schema diff captures something Jaccard cannot.

observations.description: Mock server produces zero response-time variance, making behavioral signals useless
observations.evidence: All client validation rates are 0.0 for profiles A and B. Profile C rates are low (0.0-0.093) because mock always returns data matching schema types.

observations.description: Schema diff is negatively correlated with Jaccard (r=-0.590), confirming they capture complementary structural information
observations.evidence: However, this complementarity does not solve the magnitude confound: the diff still cannot threshold-able discriminate optional_field_addition noise from add_field drift.

validity_notes: Mock server returns deterministic responses matching schema types; cannot test whether real HTTP servers introduce correlated schema-response changes
Schema diff weights (1.0 added/removed, 0.5 type, 0.3 required, 0.2 enum) are fixed but could be tuned; however, the optional_field_addition scaling issue is structural and not weight-dependent
40 conditions (4 sizes x 10 patterns) with 30 samples each provide 1200 total measurements; all variance was zero (deterministic computation), making statistical tests unnecessary
Type-aware validation (C4) cannot be fairly tested in this mock setup because server always conforms to schema; real API drift would require mismatched server responses
No external dependencies; pure computation on synthetic schemas

unresolved.question: Can a threshold be found that discriminates optional_field_addition noise from add_field drift in the specific setting where optional additions are bounded (e.g., max 2 fields per update)?
unresolved.why_unresolved: Experiment tested unbounded optional additions (10% of schema size). A bounded version might pass C2 but would narrow the mechanism's applicability.
unresolved.suggested_next_action: Re-run with bounded noise (max 2 optional fields) to test bounded-noise tolerance

unresolved.question: Would type-aware validation detect drift if the server does NOT always conform to the schema (real-world mismatch scenario)?
unresolved.why_unresolved: Mock server always returns schema-conformant data. Real API drift includes server-side non-conformance that type validation would catch.
unresolved.suggested_next_action: Test with mock server that returns stale data after schema change

unresolved.question: Does the 0.37 discrimination gap (drift=0.96 vs noise=0.59) provide useful lift over Jaccard alone (r=-0.59 suggests some complementarity)?
unresolved.why_unresolved: Experiment did not directly compare AUC of schema-diff-only vs Jaccard-only classifiers.
unresolved.suggested_next_action: Compute ROC curves for both signals and compare AUCs
